No, that is not accurate. In Switzerland, the L-permit (temporary residence permit) is indeed required for foreign nationals who wish to work in the country. However, the duration and conditions of the permit depend on the nature of the work and the length of stay.

For short-term assignments, such as a two-week project, the requirement for an L-permit can vary based on the specific circumstances and agreements between Switzerland and the individual's home country. Generally, short-term assignments lasting up to 90 days within a 180-day period may be covered under a different category, such as a short-stay visa for business purposes.

It is important to note that the specific regulations and requirements can be complex and may vary depending on factors such as the nationality of the individual, the nature of the work, and bilateral agreements between countries. Therefore, it is advisable to consult the official Swiss immigration authorities or seek legal advice to determine the specific requirements for a particular situation.
